title: Checkpoint: Shakespeare and the Novel
objective: After this level you can explain why Shakespeare's plays and the first novels changed what stories could do.
summary: Seven years after Shakespeare died, his fellow actors printed 36 plays in the First Folio (1623), saving 18. From the Globe to Austen, stage and page learned to let you hear a mind.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 finale: half of Shakespeare's plays nearly vanished.
cards.body: This chapter ran from a penny standing place at the Globe to a novel that trusts you to catch the joke. Here it is in order, then the book that saved Viola and Rosalind, then what the stage and the novel each learned to do.

events.label: The Globe opens on London's Bankside
The First Folio collects 36 of Shakespeare's plays

cards.headline: The book that saved 18 plays
cards.body: Shakespeare died in 1616. Seven years later, in 1623, his fellow actors John Heminges and Henry Condell, partners in the King's Men, gathered 36 of his plays into the First Folio. Eighteen had never been printed before, among them Macbeth, The Tempest, As You Like It and Twelfth Night. Without it, Rosalind's disguise and Viola's knot might have been lost forever.

cards.headline: Stage and page
cards.body: Look at what this chapter's writers learned to do. On a bare stage, a soliloquy let a whole crowd hear a character think alone. On the page, Austen's narration slipped into a character's voice without a word of speech. Meanwhile prose learned new tricks: Cervantes parodied the romances, Defoe's castaway posed as a real memoir, and Swift's satire held a whole society up to ridicule. And "first recorded in Shakespeare" turned out to mean the earliest written use found so far.

questions.prompt: Who gathered Shakespeare's plays into the First Folio of 1623?

options.label: Shakespeare himself, just before he died
options.rationale: He died in 1616, seven years earlier.

options.label: His fellow actors John Heminges and Henry Condell
Arthur Brooke, his source for Romeo and Juliet
The owners of the Globe's galleries
options.rationale: His fellow actors of the King's Men did.

questions.explanation: Heminges and Condell, Shakespeare's fellow actors and partners in the King's Men, gathered his plays into the First Folio of 1623.

questions.prompt: Why does the First Folio matter so much?

options.label: It was the first book ever printed in English
options.rationale: Nothing in the chapter says so.

options.label: It holds Shakespeare's private letters
Eighteen of its plays had never been printed and might have been lost
It fixed the spelling of every English word
options.rationale: Nothing in the chapter says so.

questions.explanation: Eighteen of the Folio's 36 plays, including Macbeth and Twelfth Night, had never been printed before and might otherwise be lost.
